html:
A mosque by Mimar Sinan for Mihrimah Sultan, the only daughter of Suleiman the Magnificent and Hurrem Sultan. It stands on the summit of the sixth hill, near the highest point of Istanbul, just inside the Edirne Gate of the land walls. There is no foundation inscription, but the records suggest it was built from about 1563 to 1570. It is the second and larger of her two mosques; the other is at Üsküdar.

The building is a cube under a half sphere. The dome, 20 m wide and 37 m high, rests on four corner towers, and each of the four walls beneath it is a great arch filled with windows, which makes the hall one of the lightest Sinan built. Side aisles with galleries open off it through triple arcades on granite columns. The carved marble minbar is original; the painted decoration is modern. A porch of seven domed bays leads in from a courtyard ringed by the cells of a madrasa.

Earthquakes have hit it hard: in 1766 the minaret and the dome fell, and in 1894 the single minaret crashed through the roof. The 1999 Izmit earthquake damaged the dome again, and it was restored from 2007 to 2010. The complex also had a double bath, still in use, and a row of shops under the terrace. Mihrimah herself is buried at the Süleymaniye Mosque.
